title: Token pathway profiling — regression triage notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight, hands-on log for investigating recent performance regressions that manifest as increased 95th/99th token latency on hosted endpoints. Focus is on the token pathway (tokenization -> model forward -> kv cache -> postprocess) rather than whole-request variability. The goal is a repeatable triage checklist, concrete profiling commands, and an isolation/bisect plan that works during a canary comparison window.

Context and quick timeline:
- Feb 16 2025: Alerts triggered by elevated token-level p99 for model rwd-3b-v2 on hosted API region us-west1.
- Feb 16–17: Initial dashboard spike aligns with canary deploy INF-4523.
- Feb 18: Canary rolled back; incident reopened for deeper profiling.
- Feb 20–Feb 28: Multiple short runs, partial bisects; flaky signals.
- This note started 2025-02-18 and is being iterated with profiling artifacts and bisect checkpoints.

High-level investigative hypothesis tree (keep it explicit):
1) Model variant change (new weights/graph) causing different attention patterns or larger kv writes (most likely given PR timeline).
2) Serving runtime kernel selection differences causing slower matmul / flash attention path for certain sequence lengths.
3) Change in request shape distribution (tokenization differences, more long-context requests) + batching interactions.
4) Hardware/driver mismatch (CUDA driver bump on a subset of hosts).
5) Downstream post-processing (tokenizer decode, safety filters) introduced blocking calls.

Key dashboards / queries to snapshot (Grafana / Prometheus):
- panel: token_latency_percentiles (group by model, route) — query: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, route))
- panel: kv_cache_write_bytes_per_sec (per host)
- panel: kernel_choice_fallbacks_total (counter by host and kernel_name)
- panel: batch_size_distribution (percentile) and batch_wait_time_ms
- Use-preset: compare canary vs prod (label canary=true)

Immediate triage checklist (first 30–90 minutes):
- [ ] Confirm alert fingerprint: which model, which route, which region, exact metric name and query window. Copy panel JSON.
- [ ] Roll back canary if currently deployed (if SLOs degrade). Note canary ID and commit.
- [ ] Snapshot logs for 1h before and after spike window (kubectl logs + fluentd/elk request traces).
- [ ] Export sample request traces (ids) for p99 tokens where token_index > 10. Attach to ticket.
- [ ] Run quick nvprof / perf on a single host with representative load reproducer (see reproducer steps).

Reproducer: small harness to generate deterministic token sequences and measure per-token latency
- Command (local infra run, CUDA host with model pinned):
  - export MODEL=rwd-3b-v2-canary
  - python tools/repro/generate_streaming_load.py --model $MODEL --seed 42 --prompt-set tests/perf/prompts/long-tail.json --concurrency 8 --max-tokens 256 --log-token-times ~/tmp/token_times.csv
- Expected output columns: timestamp, request_id, token_index, token_ms, host, kernel_path
- Notes: include instrumentation wrapper to call runtime endpoint with ?trace_tokens=1

Profiling commands and quick captures:
- Perf counters on host (CPU-bound decode):
  - sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 30
  - sudo perf script | flamegraph.pl > cpu-flame.svg
- GPU timeline capture (short run):
  - nvprof --profile-from-start off --print-gpu-trace -f -o nvprof.out ./bin/serving-load-test --model $MODEL --steps 50
  - nsight systems: nsys profile --output nsys-sess --trace=cuda,nvtx -- ./bin/serving-load-test
- In-runtime trace flags (dev builds):
  - export RW_TRACE_KERNELS=1 RW_TRACE_KV=1 RW_PPROF_PORT=8085
  - curl http://host:8085/pprof/profile?seconds=30 for cpu profile
- Collect CUDA kernel names and durations: parse nvprof.out and aggregate by kernel name, sequence length bucket, model.

What to look for in profiles (hypothesis -> signal):
- Hyp 1 (model change): increased compute time per forward, consistent across hosts — check average GPU op time per request. If true, compare operator kernel counts with baseline.
- Hyp 2 (kernel selection): look for fallback kernels (e.g., from flash-attn to slower matmul) reported in kernel traces; check kernel selection logs emitted by runtime.
- Hyp 3 (request shapes): batch_wait_time increases correlated with % of long prompts. Compare token_index distribution in sample traces.
- Hyp 4 (drivers): only subset of hosts show slow kernel durations and have driver versions X vs Y. Cross-reference host tags.
- Hyp 5 (postprocess): CPU flame graphs show increased time in tokenizer.decode or safety filter code paths.

Bisect plan (code + infra) — keep it surgical:
- Goal: pinpoint whether regression is caused by code change (PR) or infra/driver.
- Step 0: freeze state, tag current canary and prod commits. Record commit SHAs.
- Step 1: Deploy baseline model binary to a small canary ring with current infra/driver versions (A). Run reproducible load and capture token-level latencies.
- Step 2: Swap model to prior model version (B) on same infra; compare results. If B is fine, suspect model weights/graph changes.
- Step 3: If B still slow, roll back runtime binary to previous good commit (binary X) on same hosts and retest. If performance recovers, suspect runtime regressions.
- Step 4: Partition hosts by driver version and run step 1/2 on each to catch driver-induced regressions.
- Make bisect runs small and short (5–10 minutes) but stable, and always collect full traces.

Canary comparison methodology (deterministic, low-noise):
- Use deterministic prompt set (tests/perf/prompts/regression-suite.json) seeded with RNG=42. Use identical concurrency and token limits.
- Traffic split: 5% canary if real traffic; prefer synthetic load on dedicated hosts to reduce cross-noise.
- Metrics to record: token_p50/90/95/99, kernel_time_median, kv_write_bytes, batch_wait_ms, pprof cpu/gpu profiles, request traces for top-100 slow token samples.
- Keep experiment window >= 10 minutes; discard first 60s as warmup.

Artifacts to collect per run (store in ticket INF-4523):
- token_times.csv (reproducer), nvprof.out, nsys-sess.qs, cpu-flame.svg, grafana-snapshots JSON, sample request traces (IDs), host list and driver versions, runtime binary SHA, model SHA, serving config (batcher, max_batch_size).

Common pitfalls and lessons learned from previous regressions:
- Tiny differences in quantization config lead to different kernel selections. Always include quantization profile in artifact set.
- Telemetry gap: kernel selection logs were disabled in prod in early 2024 — we added RW_TRACE_KERNELS flag but forgot to flip on for canary. Double-check flags.
- Batching interactions: a small increase in average prompt length can push batcher into pathological case where it waits longer for a large request, exposing tail latency. Use batch_wait_ms histograms.

Short term action items (owners + ETA):
- Priya: run deterministic reproducer across 3 hosts and upload nvprof + nsys captures to ticket (ETA: 2025-03-03).
- Ethan: add a Grafana comparison dashboard that diffs canary vs prod percentiles (ETA: 2025-02-21).
- Maya: grep runtime logs for any kernel fallback messages for the suspect timeframe and attach examples (ETA: 2025-02-22).
- Omar: validate driver versions on hosts in us-west1 and flag mismatches (ETA: 2025-02-20).

Notes to self / open questions:
- Are there any A/B experiments that changed prompt preprocessing or safety filters around Feb 15–17? (check product change log)
- Could the scheduler heuristics have been tweaked? Confirm config commits in infra repo.
- Is there correlation with nightly maintenance windows that run backups (I/O noise)? Check SRE notes.

Appendix: quick grep snippets and helper commands:
- Gather host drivers and runtime versions across cluster:
  - kubectl get pods -l app=runtime -o custom-columns=HOST:.spec.nodeName,IMAGE:.spec.containers[0].image --all-namespaces | sort | uniq -c
  - for n in $(kubectl get nodes -o name); do ssh $n "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader"; done > drivers.txt
- Extract slow token traces from logs (fluentd):
  - jq '. | select(.metric=="token_latency" and .percentile>=99)' logs.jsonl | jq '{time:.ts, req:.request_id, token_index:.token_index, host:.host}' > slow_tokens.json

End — iterative notes will be appended here as we gather traces and bisect results.

Quick changelog for this doc:
- 2025-02-18: initial draft, hypothesis and checklist (Priya)
- 2025-02-20: added reproducer and profiling commands (Ethan)
- 2025-03-02: added canary methodology and artifact checklist (Priya)
